about: Ask-your-library eval: questions over the golden sample docs (packages/core/test/golden, imported into a scratch library). An answer is right when every regex in `answer` matches it (case-insensitive). Its citations are right when every quote is really in the source it names and at least one comes from a source in `sources` and matches `evidence`. The `absent` questions aren't covered by any golden doc: right means the answer says so and cites nothing. Most are near misses, a person or topic the docs do cover but not the fact asked (Ebbinghaus is there, his birth year isn't; a 90% target is there, FSRS's default isn't), which is where a grounded answer is most tempted to stretch. The `hard` questions are scored on their own line: `paraphrase` ones share few words with the passage that answers them, `follow-up` ones need the `earlier` turns to make sense, `reading` ones say "this" with `reading` open, and `two-source` ones (`all_sources`) must cite every source in `sources`. Absent questions with `outside` patterns have a settled answer the reply must get right from the web or general knowledge.
